q: Which Act introduced the Communal Electorate System?
explanation: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced communal representation through separate electorates for Muslims. It 'legalised communalism' and made Lord Minto the 'father of the communal electorate'. The 1919 and 1935 Acts only extended the principle to other groups.

notes.text: > "Which Act introduced separate / communal electorates (communal representation)?" → **Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto)** – not 1892, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford) or 1935, which only extended it.

q: Which of the following is one of the salient features of the Lucknow Pact, 1916?
options: The Congress and Muslim League would share power in Legislative Councils
The Congress accepted the system of separate electorates based on religion
The Congress and Muslim League would fight for complete independence
A working committee was established by the Congress to run day to day affairs
key_text: The Congress accepted the system of separate electorates based on religion
explanation: By the Lucknow Pact the Congress accepted the separate electorates given to Muslims by the 1909 Act. There was no power-sharing deal, no demand for complete independence (only self-government) and the Working Committee came in 1920.

notes.text: - **Main concession:** the **Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims** – the **first time (1916)** the Congress did so; Muslims got a **fixed proportion of seats** (weightage).

q: Who ordered the killing of Alluri Sitarama Raju
explanation: Alluri Sitarama Raju was shot dead on 7 May 1924 on the orders of Major Goodall. Rutherford was the Special Commissioner, not the officer at the shooting.

q: The first attack of Alluri Sitaramaraju on?
explanation: The rebellion began with the attack on Chintapalli police station on 22 August 1922 to procure arms; Krishnadevipeta and Rajavommangi followed, Annavaram came in 1923.
